submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires on the noun ' health' / ' Health' (weakly ' fitness', ' healthcare') when it stands as a bare head noun directly after a determiner, possessive, 'of', 'other' or a generic/evaluative adjective (e.g. 'protect the health of', 'the best health care', 'other health professionals', 'Department of Health'), and is near-silent when the immediately preceding word is a domain-specifying modifier that forms a fixed compound with it ('mental', 'human', 'animal', 'reproductive', 'occupational', 'general', 'World Health'); it never fires on related words such as 'medical', 'safety', 'care' or 'wealth'.

Patient safety culture (PSC) represents a key component of the quality of care offered by healthcare professionals. Therefore, it is crucial to understand the factors that influence the implementation of a safe culture. This study explored the knowledge and attitudes of healthcare professionals in Kuwait towards the factors that might affect the PSC. A qualitative study using semi-structured interviews with healthcare professionals was conducted between February and June 2018 at two major hospitals in Kuwait. Both hospitals had been accredited and have been applying the safety programmes recommended by the Kuwaiti Ministry of Health

The establishment of a radioactive waste disposal facility in Western Australia for low level waste.
The Radiation Health Section of the Health Department of Western Australia has been a repository for unwanted radioactive sources for many years. They had been placed in the radioactive store located on the Queen Elizabeth II Medical Centre Campus. After a collection period of more than 20 years the storage facilities of the Radiation Health Section were nearing capacity. A decision was made to relocate these sources into a permanent near surface burial facility. Following extensive community consultation and site investigations, waste originating in Western Australia was disposed of at Mt Walton (East), 80 km North East of Koolyanobbing
